description: Use this when the user wants a decision tree checked without a drawing, for example "do my probabilities add up to 1" or "is anything missing in this tree". Takes the same outline or node list and objective as make_decision_tree. Returns, for each chance node, the sum of its branch probabilities as a fraction and whether it is 1; end nodes without a payoff; probabilities on decision options; payoffs on nodes that have branches; single-option decisions; duplicate branch names; and the depth and node counts against the limits. When nothing is wrong it also gives the root expected value. Refuses a tree it is unable to read (unknown parent, a loop, two roots, over the limits), naming the line or id. Does not draw the tree or make files. Do not use it to estimate probabilities.

nodes.description: The tree as a JSON list instead of outline: each node has id, parent (not for the root), label, and p, cost or payoff as needed, e.g. [{"id":"r","label":"Launch?"},{"id":"a","parent":"r","label":"Do not launch","payoff":0}].

cost.description: Amount paid on this branch, e.g. 200.

id.description: Unique id of the node, e.g. "n1".

label.description: Short name of the node or of the branch into it, e.g. "Strong demand".

p.description: Probability of this branch when the parent is a chance node, e.g. 0.6, "1/3" or "35%".

parent.description: Id of the parent node; leave out for the root only, e.g. "n1".

payoff.description: Value at an end node, e.g. 1000 or -300.

type.description: decision, chance or end. Optional: inferred from the branches as in the outline.

objective.description: max (default): choose the option with the highest expected value, for profit or gain. min: choose the lowest, when payoffs are costs, losses or time. Example: max.

outline.description:
The tree as indented text, one node per line, children indented under their parent (spaces or tabs, "- " bullets allowed). The first line is the root. Fields after the label: p=<probability> on branches of a chance node, cost=<amount> on any branch, payoff=<amount> on end nodes; separate them with spaces or "|". A node whose branches have p is a chance node, a node with branches and no p is a decision, a node with no branches is an end node; "Decision:", "Chance:" or "End:" before a label states the type. Numbers: decimals (0.35, -1,200.50, $300), fractions (1/3), and percents for p (35%). Up to 300 nodes. Example: "Launch? | decision
  Launch | cost=200
    Strong demand | p=0.6 | payoff=1000
    Weak demand | p=0.4 | payoff=-300
  Do not launch | payoff=0".

name: check_tree
title: Check decision tree
